title: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky calls for more AI products for regular people
excerpt: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said it's in Silicon Valley's best interest to change Americans' minds about AI. He has an idea how to do it.
content_html:
Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky thinks Silicon Valley holds the answer to AI's growing public perception problem: build things for regular people.

Chesky, a major proponent of AI, acknowledged AI backlash among Americans in an interview on the Yahoo Finance podcast "Power Players with Brian Sozzi" published this week. Part of the reason for it, he said, is the kinds of AI products that Silicon Valley is and isn't shipping.

"I think part of it's a narrative issue that we're not talking about AI correctly," he said. "But part of it is we need to actually be developing more products that just regular people can use and say, 'I love AI because AI allows me to have a doctor on demand and I can't have that. I can't afford that.' And so I think we need more regular things."

Chesky said that compared to when he started Airbnb 18 years ago, many founders now seem to be "afraid" to make consumer-facing products. He said in the last batch of companies at the startup accelerator Y Combinator, where he is on the board, 159 out of 175 were enterprise, not consumer.

"It's in Silicon Valley's interest for us to develop consumer applications that improve people's lives," he said. "You know why? Because regular people in the United States do not like AI. I'm making a generalization. But if you look at polling of AI, the concept of AI is not popular outside of Silicon Valley, and yet this is a technology that can help so many people's lives."

A Pew Research Center report in June found that 40% of US adults believed the impact of AI on society over the next 20 years would be negative, while only 16% believed it would be positive.

The rising AI resistance has put some Silicon Valley figures on the offensive. Several AI companies have put out rainbow-filled, feel-good ads in an attempt to flip the script on Americans' doom-and-gloom fears about an AI-ridden future. Tech CEOs are also writing lengthy manifestos about what the future with AI will look like, including Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg's 6,500-word screed published this week titled "The Future is for Everyone."

Airbnb declined to provide additional comment when reached by Business Insider.

content_html_zh:
Airbnb 首席执行官布莱恩·切斯基 (Brian Chesky) 认为，硅谷拥有解决人工智能日益严重的公众认知问题的答案：为普通人创造东西。

人工智能的主要支持者切斯基在本周发布的雅虎财经播客“布莱恩·索齐的强力玩家”采访中承认美国人对人工智能的强烈反对。 他说，部分原因是硅谷正在生产和没有生产的人工智能产品种类。

“我认为部分原因在于我们没有正确谈论人工智能，”他说。 “但部分原因是我们实际上需要开发更多普通人可以使用的产品，并说，‘我喜欢人工智能，因为人工智能让我可以按需请医生，而我却不能这样做。 我负担不起。 所以我认为我们需要更多常规的事情。”

Chesky表示，与18年前创办Airbnb时相比，许多创始人现在似乎“害怕”制造面向消费者的产品。 他表示，在创业加速器 Y Combinator（他是该公司的董事会成员）的最后一批公司中，175 家公司中有 159 家是企业，而不是消费者。

“开发改善人们生活的消费者应用程序符合硅谷的利益，”他说。 “你知道为什么吗？ 因为美国老百姓不喜欢人工智能。 我正在做一个概括。 但如果你看一下人工智能的民意调查，就会发现人工智能的概念在硅谷之外并不流行，但这是一项可以帮助很多人生活的技术。”

皮尤研究中心 6 月份的一份报告发现，40% 的美国成年人认为人工智能在未来 20 年对社会的影响将是负面的，而只有 16% 的人认为它将是积极的。

日益高涨的人工智能阻力让一些硅谷人士发起了攻势。 几家人工智能公司推出了充满彩虹、让人感觉良好的广告，试图扭转美国人对人工智能未来的悲观恐惧。 科技公司的首席执行官们也在撰写关于人工智能未来的长篇宣言，其中包括 Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格本周发表的 6,500 字的长篇大论，题为“未来属于每个人”。
